nodes.summary: Let $k > 1$, let $A_n$ be the anti-recurrence numbers of the linear form $(1, \dots, 1)$ of length $k$, and put $i = \lfloor k/2 \rfloor$ and $\kappa = k^2 + 1$. Then for every $n \ge 1$, $A_n$ lies in the interval $[\kappa(n - 1) + 1, \kappa n]$, and $A_n \equiv ik + c \pmod{\kappa}$ for some natural number $c$ with $1 \le c \le k$ if $k$ is even and $i + 1 \le c \le i + k$ if $k$ is odd.
nodes.title: Intervals and residues of the anti-$k$-bonacci numbers

nodes.summary: For $n \ge 1$, $A_n$ is the first entry of the $n$-th triple $(A_n, B_n, C_n)$ of the anti-Fibonacci construction: $A_1 = 1$, and for $n \ge 2$, $A_n$ is the least positive integer that is not among the values $A_k$, $B_k$, $C_k$ with $1 \le k < n$. At $n = 0$ the definition gives $A_0 = A_1 = 1$.
nodes.title: First summands of the anti-Fibonacci construction

nodes.summary: For $n \ge 1$, $B_n$ is the second entry of the $n$-th triple $(A_n, B_n, C_n)$ of the anti-Fibonacci construction: $B_1 = 2$, and for $n \ge 2$, $B_n$ is the second smallest positive integer that is not among the values $A_k$, $B_k$, $C_k$ with $1 \le k < n$. At $n = 0$ the definition gives $B_0 = B_1 = 2$.
nodes.title: Second summands of the anti-Fibonacci construction

nodes.summary: For $n \ge 1$, the anti-Fibonacci number $X_n = C_n$ is the third entry of the $n$-th triple $(A_n, B_n, C_n)$ of the anti-Fibonacci construction, so $C_n = A_n + B_n$ and $C_1 = 3$. At $n = 0$ the definition gives $C_0 = C_1 = 3$.

nodes.summary: Let $A_n$ be the anti-recurrence numbers of the linear form $a = (1, 2)$ (the anti-Pell numbers), let $B_m$ be its non-anti-recurrence numbers, and put $B^1_n = B_{2n-1}$ and $B^2_n = B_{2n}$. nodes.summary: Let $c$ and $d$ be natural numbers. If none of the coefficients of $x^0, x^1, \dots, x^{c+d}$ in the integer polynomial $(x-1)^c (x+1)^d$ is divisible by $3$, then there are natural numbers $i > j$ such that $c + d + 1$ equals $3^j$, $2 \cdot 3^j$, $3^i + 3^j$ or $2 \cdot 3^i + 3^j$.

nodes.summary: A positive integer $p$ is an *upper Wythoff number* when the letter at index $p - 1$ (indices start at $0$) of the infinite Fibonacci word $0100101001001\ldots$ is $1$; that is, the upper Wythoff numbers are the positions of the letter $1$ in the Fibonacci word counted from one. A positive integer $x$ is an *unsum* (OEIS A260317) if there are no upper Wythoff numbers $p < q$ with $p + q = x$.

nodes.title: Digit sums of the words between markers

nodes.summary: Let $g_0, g_1, g_2, \ldots$ be the gaps between consecutive unsums, and call an index $i \ge 10$ with $g_i = 2$ a marker. Let $m_0 < m_1 < m_2 < \cdots$ be the markers in increasing order. For each $j$, the $j$-th word between markers is $g_{m_j + 1} g_{m_j + 2} \cdots g_{m_{j+1} - 1}$, the word of the gaps strictly between the $j$-th and the $(j+1)$-th marker.
nodes.title: Words between markers in the unsum gap sequence

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
